Die Abteilung Compute- und Speichersysteme der Leibniz Universität IT Services bietet im Rahmen des Dienstes Scientific Computing einen zentralen High-Performance Computing (HPC)-Rechencluster an. Ihre Stelle im Überblick Zur Unterstützung des neu aufzubauenden Verbundvorhabens „Lower Saxony Digital Science Support Space (DS³)“ im Rahmen der Hochschule.digital Niedersachsen suchen wir zwei engagierte Mitarbeiterinnen oder Mitarbeiter mit nachgewiesenem Interesse an den Bereichen High-Performance Computing (HPC), Künstliche Intelligenz (KI) und dem Betrieb der hierfür erforderlichen Infrastruktur und Services. Ziel des vom Land Niedersachsen geförderten Kooperationsprojekts DS³ ist der flächendeckende Ausbau von forschungsnahen IT-Infrastrukturen und Dienstleistungen an niedersächsischen Hochschulen. Als einer der tragenden Standorte wird das LUIS im Rahmen des Projekts eine Tier-3-HPC-Infrastruktur bereitstellen, betreiben und die Forschenden bei deren Nutzung unterstützen. Sie arbeiten in einem Team aus erfahrenen Beschäftigten sowohl eigenständig als auch gemeinsam schwerpunktmäßig an folgenden Aufgaben: Projektmanagement und lokale Koordination des Verbundvorhabens DS³ am Standort LUIS sowie die Zusammenarbeit mit den beteiligten Partnerinstitutionen in Niedersachsen Aufbau, Konfiguration, Administration und Wartung des Tier-3-HPC-Clusters des LUIS sowie der dazugehörigen Storage-, GPU-beschleunigten Hardware- und Monitoring-Systeme Technische Unterstützung und Beratung von Nutzern und Forschenden bei der effizienten Nutzung der HPC-Ressourcen, dem Deployment von KI-Werkzeugen und Large Language Models (LLMs), dem Performance Engineering sowie bei der Skalierung von HPC-Rechenprozessen und Machine Learning-Workloads Mitarbeit beim Aufbau und der Etablierung nachhaltiger Services im Bereich der forschungsnahen IT-Infrastruktur für datenintensive HPC- und KI-Anwendungen innerhalb des DS³-Netzwerks Erstellung von Dokumentationsmaterial für verschiedene Zielgruppen sowie die Vertretung des LUIS-Teilprojekts in projektinternen Arbeitsgruppen Wen suchen wir? Voraussetzung für die Einstellung ist ein abgeschlossenes wissenschaftliches Hochschulstudium, vorzugsweise in einem MINT-Studiengang (oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation) mit einschlägiger Berufserfahrung im HPC- oder KI-Umfeld. Erfahrung im Linux-basierten Einsatz von Cluster-Technologien wie Workload-Managementsystemen (z. B. Slurm) sowie verteilten Dateisystemen (z. B. NFS, Lustre) für datenintensive Anwendungen wird vorausgesetzt. Kenntnisse im Bereich von Objektspeichersystemen (z. B. Ceph, S3) sind hierbei von Vorteil. Gute Kenntnisse in den Skriptsprachen Python und Bash zur Automatisierung sowie Vertrautheit mit modernen Monitoring-Lösungen für Cluster-Systeme (z. B. Prometheus und Grafana) und die Bereitschaft zur Erstellung präziser technischer Dokumentationen werden vorausgesetzt. Kenntnisse in höheren Programmiersprachen, idealerweise C++, C oder Fortran, sind hierbei erwünscht. Sie haben Kenntnisse zu Containertechnologien (z. B. Apptainer/Singularity) zur Bereitstellung portabler KI- und HPC-Anwendungen. Idealerweise bringen Sie zudem Erfahrungen mit Virtualisierungsplattformen (z. B. KVM, oVirt, OpenStack) mit. Erfahrung im Umgang mit Konfigurations- und Management-Werkzeugen (z. B. Kickstart/PXE, EasyBuild, Pacemaker/Corosync, Puppet/Ansible) wird erwartet. Praktische Erfahrung mit KI-Systemen, dem Deployment von Large Language Models auf GPU-beschleunigter Hardware sowie Kenntnisse in der Versionsverwaltung Git sind hierbei von Vorteil. Regelmäßige Fortbildungen helfen Ihnen, Ihre persönlichen Kompetenzen gezielt weiterzuentwickeln. Sie sind eine aufgeschlossene Person mit guten kommunikativen Fähigkeiten, handeln lösungs- und zielorientiert und bringen eine hohe Selbstorganisation, Belastbarkeit sowie Teamfähigkeit mit. Sehr gute Englisch- und gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift werden vorausgesetzt, um unsere internationalen Nutzerinnen und Nutzer optimal zu betreuen. Die Leibniz Universität Hannover setzt sich für Chancengleichheit und Diversität ein. Ziel ist es, das Potenzial aller zu nutzen und Chancen zu eröffnen. Wir begrüßen daher Bewerbungen von allen Interessierten unabhängig von deren Geschlecht, Nationalität, ethnischer Herkunft, Religion oder Weltanschauung, Behinderung, Alter, sexueller Orientierung und Identität. Wir streben eine gleichmäßige Verteilung der Beschäftigten und einen Abbau der Unterrepräsentanz im Sinne des Niedersächsischen Gleichberechtigungsgesetzes (NGG) an. Daher freuen wir uns, wenn sich auch Frauen auf die o. g. Stelle bewerben. Menschen mit einer Schwerbehinderung werden bei gleicher Qualifikation bevorzugt. Was bieten wir? Wir setzen auf familienfreundliche und flexible Arbeitszeitmodelle. Teilzeit, Mobiles Arbeiten und Homeoffice sind nach Absprache möglich. Wir unterstützen die Vereinbarkeit von Familie und Beruf mit Angeboten der Kindernotfallbetreuung und Ferienbetreuung sowie Eltern-Kind-Büros und beraten individuell zu Familien- und Pflegeaufgaben. Wir bieten als Rechenzentrum der Leibniz Universität Hannover einen interessanten und abwechslungsreichen Arbeitsplatz mit einer freundlichen und wertschätzenden Atmosphäre. We combine software and systems engineering: we build the automation and observability that run these services, define and defend service-level objectives, write the standard operating procedures (SOPs) the platform runs on, and lead the response when things go wrong. We also prove resilience rather than assume it, through chaos engineering and platform-level disaster-recovery fire drills, and we harden the platform's security and strengthen its compliance controls. Design and implement systems that continually improve the reliability, efficiency and security of the compute and storage platform, from architecture through to production code. Working knowledge of datacenter networking: L3 fabrics, BGP, load balancing, DNS. Chaos engineering tools such as Chaos Mesh, LitmusChaos or Gremlin, or a fault-injection framework you built. Security hardening in practice: CIS benchmarks, OS and Kubernetes hardening, secrets management, policy-as-code (OPA, Kyverno). Running a public cloud service with external customers, SLAs and compliance audits (ISO 27001, SOC 2, MTCS). GPU servers or AI workloads on the compute and storage you run.

review_candidates.company: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies - IFRC
review_candidates.description: SRI Executive Search has been contracted by the IFRC to assist with the search for an exceptional candidate to fill the position of Regional Director (Asia Pacific, Europe and MENA). About the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191 member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability. IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe. IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles. For more information, visit www.ifrc.org/. Role Purpose The Regional Director leads IFRC’s work in the region and is a member of the Global Leadership Team (GLT). Under the overall leadership of the Secretary General and the direct line management of the USG-NSDC, the Regional Director provides vision, leadership, strategic guidance, and effective management of the IFRC Secretariat’s work and resources in the region of assignment, including in the relevant strategic areas of National Society development, operations coordination, partnerships and humanitarian diplomacy, and management. The Regional Director also coordinates activities closely with the Executive Office; Under-Secretary General, Humanitarian Diplomacy and Digitalization (HDD); and the Under-Secretary General, People and Strategy (PAS), to ensure effective coordination across the IFRC Secretariat. Major Duties and Responsibilities Champion and ensure effective and agile model of leadership working as one IFRC. Within the framework of IFRC’s Strategy 2030, the Agenda for Renewal, and the IFRC Way of Working, and under the guidance of the USG-NSDC, the Regional Director is responsible for providing strategic leadership across the region and ensuring impactful support to National Societies. This includes strengthening their capacities to reduce and address fragility, enhance resilience, and ensure effective readiness and preparedness for crises. As a member of the Global Leadership Team, the Regional Director is responsible for ensuring that IFRC operates as one organization, maximizing and connecting capacities, expertise, and resources at delegations, and global levels. The Regional Director will provide leadership for the implementation of the Agenda for Renewal and the IFRC Way of Working, translating these directions into effective regional and country-level action in support of the ambitions and objectives of Strategy 2030. Ensure delivery of the five strategic priorities underpinned by the five strategic shifts of IFRC Renewal and support National Societies in advancing the implementation of Strategy 2030 Ensure that the IFRC secretariat efforts are focused on mobilizing investments in delivering relevant and effective programs and services by national societies in the areas of: Response – in scale, speed and scope that is comprehensive and people focused Resilience – focusing on climate and environmental challenges, health and wellbeing and migration and identity, and Respect - for our fundamental principles and our work on values, power and inclusion. Lead the implementation of the five Strategic shifts of the IFRC Renewal in the region, ensuring that deepening localisation and accountability; sharpening humanitarian focus, influence, and impact; intensifying trust and collaboration; accelerating digital transformation and AI adoption; and fostering a more innovative and agile Secretariat are fully integrated into Regional and Delegation plans and translated into measurable results. Place People and National Societies at the centre of IFRC planning, decision-making, and operational delivery, ensuring that support reflects their priorities and capacities while strengthening accountability to communities, agility, principled conduct, partnerships, and alignment with IFRC statutory instruments and General Assembly resolutions. Ensure that the Global teams and Delegations operate as one IFRC system, effectively connecting delegations and global capacities, tools, standards, and resources to strengthen preparedness, readiness, and response capabilities of National Societies and IFRC offices and maximize collective impact. Provide strategic oversight of country-level capacity, resources, and delegated authority, ensuring implementation of the target of at least 75% of financial resources at country level, appropriate delegation of authority, robust first- and second-line oversight, transparency and accountability, and adherence to technical quality standards while maximizing the effective use of resources. Ensure National Society Development Provide strategic leadership and direction for National Society development and strengthening across the region, ensuring that IFRC regional and country teams prioritize investment in stronger, more sustainable, accountable, and trusted National Societies as critical local humanitarian actors and partners of choice. Lead strategic engagement with National Society leadership, maintaining regular dialogue to understand priorities and concerns, identify opportunities for collaboration, and advance institutional development, including integrity, safeguarding, systems strengthening, financial sustainability and domestic income generation, branch development, and stronger relationships with public authorities. Direct and oversee efforts to strengthen the institutional foundations and effectiveness of National Societies, including their legal base and auxiliary role, Unified Plans and operational plans, and the development and implementation of policies, systems, programmes, and capacity-strengthening initiatives that enhance the effectiveness, efficiency, accountability, engagement, and trust of IFRC membership. Drive coordinated and evidence-based investment in National Society development, ensuring consistent use of the National Society Investment Dashboard across regional and delegation teams to identify priorities, align technical and financial resources, coordinate partner support, and establish appropriate investment mechanisms at country and regional levels. Strengthen leadership, volunteering, youth, and branch development across the region, including regional leadership-development initiatives, mentoring future leaders, advancing women in leadership, promoting strategic foresight and leadership learning, and ensuring that all teams actively contribute technical and financial resources to agreed strategies and plans. Provide strategic leadership, management, and coordination for high-quality support to National Societies, ensuring that relevant internal and external analysis informs strategic alignment across the region and that IFRC support enables National Societies to strengthen community resilience and address the needs of vulnerable people across health, social, economic, and other programme areas, consistent with priorities established by the Secretary General and under the overall guidance of the USG-NSDC. Lead Strategic and Operational Coordination Responsible for ensuring coordination is integral component for the IFRC Renewal in action across the region: Membership Cooperation, including IFRC Secretariat and its member NSs implement the IFRC Way of Working and use IFRC policies as key reference guidance to work effectively as a network. Movement Coordination, including IFRC, its member NSs and the ICRC implement the Seville Agreement 2.0 and its tools. Coordination with external partners, such as governments, international organizations, civil society organizations, NGOs, private sector entities, and other stakeholders involved in humanitarian work. Ensure that Federation policies, procedures, guidelines, and quality standards are properly implemented, and adhered by staff and all partners with whom the Federation works. Ensure adequate cooperation and coordination in all programmes and operations ensuring the most effective and efficient mobilisation and utilisation of resources. Build effective cooperation and partnerships with a wide range of partners and stakeholders in government, civil society, academia, and the private sector, and where appropriate engage with the UN Country Team and other humanitarian actors. Ensure that the Cooperation Policy and other Policies are effectively implemented and monitored. Provide strategic leadership for IFRC engagement and dialogue with the ICRC across the region, fostering strong coordination, joint context analysis, and timely identification of Movement-wide opportunities, challenges, and risks, and promoting coherent and complementary action in support of National Societies and the wider Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement. Lead Effective Humanitarian Diplomacy Provide strategic leadership for purpose driven humanitarian diplomacy, communications, and external relations across the region, translating IFRC global strategies and positions into regional priorities and establishing consistent protocols and approaches for external engagement across the Regional Office and Country Delegations. Build and strengthen strategic partnerships and broad alliances that advance shared humanitarian priorities and position IFRC and its network of National Societies as partners of choice, including proactive engagement with regional intergovernmental organizations, international financial institutions, embassies, academia, civil society, and other influential regional and international actors. Represent and advocate for IFRC positions on key humanitarian and development issues in high-level regional, Movement, and external forums, contributing regional perspectives to Federation-wide policy development and ensuring that the priorities and ambitions of National Societies are effectively promoted and supported. Champion the Fundamental Principles and a principled approach to humanitarian action across the region, ensuring that IFRC teams lead by example, consistently apply Federation-wide standards and guidance, and work with National Societies to address stigma, discrimination, social exclusion, and violence while contributing to peace and social harmony. Ensure effective regional advocacy and strategic alignment around National Society priorities, enabling Country Delegations and the Regional Office to support, promote, disseminate, and advocate for National Society humanitarian and development priorities, plans, and actions with relevant partners and decision-makers. Drive stronger information management and digital transformation in support of humanitarian action and influence, ensuring timely and relevant analysis and reporting for IFRC senior leadership, humanitarian diplomacy, communications, and decision-making, while supporting Federation-wide digital transformation to strengthen IFRC's capacity to serve National Societies and remain fit for the future. Ensure Agility Drive an agile, adaptive, and accountable approach to IFRC operations across the region, strengthening systems, processes, and ways of working to improve responsiveness, effectiveness, quality, and impact in support of National Societies. Ensure appropriate capacity and resources are positioned at country level, enabling IFRC teams to provide effective support to National Societies on core priorities and ensuring that financial resources are allocated strategically to maximize country-level impact. Exercise sound judgment, creativity, and flexibility in implementing IFRC decisions and strengthening coordination, ensuring effective engagement with National Societies, the wider Movement, donors, humanitarian actors, the private sector, and other relevant stakeholders. Ensure Transparency and Accountability Ensure overall accountability, effective management, and organizational oversight across the region, including the Regional Office and Country and Cluster Delegations, maintaining accountability to affected people and communities, National Societies, donors, partners, and other stakeholders, and fostering a culture of transparency, learning, responsibility, and continuous improvement. Provide strategic oversight of IFRC risk, business continuity, legal compliance, and duty of care, ensuring that strategic and operational decisions are informed by effective risk management; that Risk Registers and Business Continuity Plans are maintained and regularly updated; and that applicable legal obligations, status agreements, and institutional responsibilities are consistently upheld. Ensure sound financial stewardship and effective management of IFRC resources across the region, including robust budget planning, expenditure control, financial oversight, and delivery within approved budget

The ideal candidate can independently manage payment integrations, investigate complex technical issues, collaborate effectively with business and development teams and external providers, and identify opportunities to improve payment performance and reliability. Analyze PSP API documentation, integration requirements, and payment workflows to identify optimal technical solutions. Collaborate with development and QA teams throughout the integration lifecycle, from initial analysis and technical specification to testing and production release. Identify potential integration risks, technical limitations, and dependencies at early stages and coordinate integration activities with external PSPs and internal stakeholders to ensure timely and high-quality delivery. Support the implementation of new payment features and improvements to existing integrations and maintain comprehensive technical documentation, integration specifications, and payment flow descriptions. Validate critical payment scenarios, including successful and failed transactions, timeouts, callbacks, refunds, and edge cases. Investigate production issues by analyzing API requests/responses, transaction statuses, callbacks, and application logs. Strong understanding of payment lifecycles, including payment initiation, processing, authorization, confirmation, settlement, and refunds. Solid knowledge of different payment methods, including card payments, e-wallets, bank transfers, and APMs. Understanding of payment statuses, transaction processing logic, and common payment failure scenarios. Experience analyzing PSP integration requirements and translating them into clear technical specifications. Strong understanding of REST APIs and client-server architecture. Hands-on experience working with HTTP/HTTPS, JSON, and API request/response structures. Good understanding of HTTP methods, status codes, headers, and authentication mechanisms (API keys, Bearer tokens, Basic Authentication, HMAC signatures). Practical experience using Postman or similar API testing tools. Understanding of synchronous and asynchronous communication patterns. Knowledge of webhooks/callbacks and their role in payment processing. Experience using browser Developer Tools (Network tab) to analyze HTTP requests and responses. Familiarity with Jira, Confluence, and technical monitoring tools. Strong analytical thinking and attention to detail. Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills. Ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams, including developers, QA engineers, product managers, business teams, and external providers. Russian and English proficiency at B2 (Upper-Intermediate) level or higher, both written and spoken. Nice to have: Understanding of the broader payments ecosystem, including payment gateways, acquirers, card schemes, settlement, and reconciliation. Experience with payment routing, cascading, and payment performance optimization. Basic SQL knowledge and experience working with Kibana/ELK, Grafana, or similar monitoring tools. Understanding of microservices architecture and message brokers (Kafka, RabbitMQ). Knowledge of PCI DSS and payment security principles. review_candidates.title: Regional Directors for IFRC
review_candidates.description: SRI Executive Search has been contracted by the IFRC to assist with the search for an exceptional candidate to fill the position of Regional Director (Asia Pacific, Europe and MENA). About the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191 member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability. IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe. IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles. For more information, visit www.ifrc.org/. Role Purpose The Regional Director leads IFRC’s work in the region and is a member of the Global Leadership Team (GLT). Under the overall leadership of the Secretary General and the direct line management of the USG-NSDC, the Regional Director provides vision, leadership, strategic guidance, and effective management of the IFRC Secretariat’s work and resources in the region of assignment, including in the relevant strategic areas of National Society development, operations coordination, partnerships and humanitarian diplomacy, and management. The Regional Director also coordinates activities closely with the Executive Office; Under-Secretary General, Humanitarian Diplomacy and Digitalization (HDD); and the Under-Secretary General, People and Strategy (PAS), to ensure effective coordination across the IFRC Secretariat. Major Duties and Responsibilities Champion and ensure effective and agile model of leadership working as one IFRC. Within the framework of IFRC’s Strategy 2030, the Agenda for Renewal, and the IFRC Way of Working, and under the guidance of the USG-NSDC, the Regional Director is responsible for providing strategic leadership across the region and ensuring impactful support to National Societies. This includes strengthening their capacities to reduce and address fragility, enhance resilience, and ensure effective readiness and preparedness for crises. As a member of the Global Leadership Team, the Regional Director is responsible for ensuring that IFRC operates as one organization, maximizing and connecting capacities, expertise, and resources at delegations, and global levels. The Regional Director will provide leadership for the implementation of the Agenda for Renewal and the IFRC Way of Working, translating these directions into effective regional and country-level action in support of the ambitions and objectives of Strategy 2030. Ensure delivery of the five strategic priorities underpinned by the five strategic shifts of IFRC Renewal and support National Societies in advancing the implementation of Strategy 2030 Ensure that the IFRC secretariat efforts are focused on mobilizing investments in delivering relevant and effective programs and services by national societies in the areas of: Response – in scale, speed and scope that is comprehensive and people focused Resilience – focusing on climate and environmental challenges, health and wellbeing and migration and identity, and Respect - for our fundamental principles and our work on values, power and inclusion. Lead the implementation of the five Strategic shifts of the IFRC Renewal in the region, ensuring that deepening localisation and accountability; sharpening humanitarian focus, influence, and impact; intensifying trust and collaboration; accelerating digital transformation and AI adoption; and fostering a more innovative and agile Secretariat are fully integrated into Regional and Delegation plans and translated into measurable results. Place People and National Societies at the centre of IFRC planning, decision-making, and operational delivery, ensuring that support reflects their priorities and capacities while strengthening accountability to communities, agility, principled conduct, partnerships, and alignment with IFRC statutory instruments and General Assembly resolutions. Ensure that the Global teams and Delegations operate as one IFRC system, effectively connecting delegations and global capacities, tools, standards, and resources to strengthen preparedness, readiness, and response capabilities of National Societies and IFRC offices and maximize collective impact. Provide strategic oversight of country-level capacity, resources, and delegated authority, ensuring implementation of the target of at least 75% of financial resources at country level, appropriate delegation of authority, robust first- and second-line oversight, transparency and accountability, and adherence to technical quality standards while maximizing the effective use of resources. Ensure National Society Development Provide strategic leadership and direction for National Society development and strengthening across the region, ensuring that IFRC regional and country teams prioritize investment in stronger, more sustainable, accountable, and trusted National Societies as critical local humanitarian actors and partners of choice. Lead strategic engagement with National Society leadership, maintaining regular dialogue to understand priorities and concerns, identify opportunities for collaboration, and advance institutional development, including integrity, safeguarding, systems strengthening, financial sustainability and domestic income generation, branch development, and stronger relationships with public authorities. Direct and oversee efforts to strengthen the institutional foundations and effectiveness of National Societies, including their legal base and auxiliary role, Unified Plans and operational plans, and the development and implementation of policies, systems, programmes, and capacity-strengthening initiatives that enhance the effectiveness, efficiency, accountability, engagement, and trust of IFRC membership. Drive coordinated and evidence-based investment in National Society development, ensuring consistent use of the National Society Investment Dashboard across regional and delegation teams to identify priorities, align technical and financial resources, coordinate partner support, and establish appropriate investment mechanisms at country and regional levels. Strengthen leadership, volunteering, youth, and branch development across the region, including regional leadership-development initiatives, mentoring future leaders, advancing women in leadership, promoting strategic foresight and leadership learning, and ensuring that all teams actively contribute technical and financial resources to agreed strategies and plans. Provide strategic leadership, management, and coordination for high-quality support to National Societies, ensuring that relevant internal and external analysis informs strategic alignment across the region and that IFRC support enables National Societies to strengthen community resilience and address the needs of vulnerable people across health, social, economic, and other programme areas, consistent with priorities established by the Secretary General and under the overall guidance of the USG-NSDC. Lead Strategic and Operational Coordination Responsible for ensuring coordination is integral component for the IFRC Renewal in action across the region: Membership Cooperation, including IFRC Secretariat and its member NSs implement the IFRC Way of Working and use IFRC policies as key reference guidance to work effectively as a network. Movement Coordination, including IFRC, its member NSs and the ICRC implement the Seville Agreement 2.0 and its tools. Coordination with external partners, such as governments, international organizations, civil society organizations, NGOs, private sector entities, and other stakeholders involved in humanitarian work. Ensure that Federation policies, procedures, guidelines, and quality standards are properly implemented, and adhered by staff and all partners with whom the Federation works. Ensure adequate cooperation and coordination in all programmes and operations ensuring the most effective and efficient mobilisation and utilisation of resources. Build effective cooperation and partnerships with a wide range of partners and stakeholders in government, civil society, academia, and the private sector, and where appropriate engage with the UN Country Team and other humanitarian actors. Ensure that the Cooperation Policy and other Policies are effectively implemented and monitored. Provide strategic leadership for IFRC engagement and dialogue with the ICRC across the region, fostering strong coordination, joint context analysis, and timely identification of Movement-wide opportunities, challenges, and risks, and promoting coherent and complementary action in support of National Societies and the wider Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement. Lead Effective Humanitarian Diplomacy Provide strategic leadership for purpose driven humanitarian diplomacy, communications, and external relations across the region, translating IFRC global strategies and positions into regional priorities and establishing consistent protocols and approaches for external engagement across the Regional Office and Country Delegations. Build and strengthen strategic partnerships and broad alliances that advance shared humanitarian priorities and position IFRC and its network of National Societies as partners of choice, including proactive engagement with regional intergovernmental organizations, international financial institutions, embassies, academia, civil society, and other influential regional and international actors. Represent and advocate for IFRC positions on key humanitarian and development issues in high-level regional, Movement, and external forums, contributing regional perspectives to Federation-wide policy development and ensuring that the priorities and ambitions of National Societies are effectively promoted and supported. Champion the Fundamental Principles and a principled approach to humanitarian action across the region, ensuring that IFRC teams lead by example, consistently apply Federation-wide standards and guidance, and work with National Societies to address stigma, discrimination, social exclusion, and violence while contributing to peace and social harmony. Ensure effective regional advocacy and strategic alignment around National Society priorities, enabling Country Delegations and the Regional Office to support, promote, disseminate, and advocate for National Society humanitarian and development priorities, plans, and actions with relevant partners and decision-makers. Drive stronger information management and digital transformation in support of humanitarian action and influence, ensuring timely and relevant analysis and reporting for IFRC senior leadership, humanitarian diplomacy, communications, and decision-making, while supporting Federation-wide digital transformation to strengthen IFRC's capacity to serve National Societies and remain fit for the future. Ensure Agility Drive an agile, adaptive, and accountable approach to IFRC operations across the region, strengthening systems, processes, and ways of working to improve responsiveness, effectiveness, quality, and impact in support of National Societies. Ensure appropriate capacity and resources are positioned at country level, enabling IFRC teams to provide effective support to National Societies on core priorities and ensuring that financial resources are allocated strategically to maximize country-level impact. Exercise sound judgment, creativity, and flexibility in implementing IFRC decisions and strengthening coordination, ensuring effective engagement with National Societies, the wider Movement, donors, humanitarian actors, the private sector, and other relevant stakeholders. Ensure Transparency and Accountability Ensure overall accountability, effective management, and organizational oversight across the region, including the Regional Office and Country and Cluster Delegations, maintaining accountability to affected people and communities, National Societies, donors, partners, and other stakeholders, and fostering a culture of transparency, learning, responsibility, and continuous improvement. Provide strategic oversight of IFRC risk, business continuity, legal compliance, and duty of care, ensuring that strategic and operational decisions are informed by effective risk management; that Risk Registers and Business Continuity Plans are maintained and regularly updated; and that applicable legal obligations, status agreements, and institutional responsibilities are consistently upheld. Ensure sound financial stewardship and effective management of IFRC resources across the region, including robust budget planning, expenditure control, financial oversight, and delivery within approved budget
